method_card.title: Relationships and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships, marriage and family life, and how to talk about future plans using the near future (ir a + infinitive) and the conditional (I would). These are among the most tested structures in writing and speaking assessments.

SpanishEnglish
la parejacouple / partner
el novio / la noviaboyfriend / girlfriend
la bodawedding
el matrimoniomarriage
casarseto get married
divorciarseto get divorced
enamorarse deto fall in love with
soltero/asingle
casado/amarried
algún díaone day
en el futuroin the future
me gustaríaI would like (conditional)
cuando sea mayorwhen I am older (Higher)
comprometerseto get engaged (Higher)

Grammar focus: near future and conditional. Near future: voy a + infinitive (e.g. Voy a casarme = I am going to get married). Conditional: add -ía endings to the infinitive (e.g. casaría, viviría, tendría). Irregular conditional stems: tendr-, podr-, querr-, har-. Me gustaría = I would like — always followed by the infinitive: Me gustaría tener dos hijos.

Note: estar casado/a uses estar because being married is a state, not a permanent identity. Contrast with ser soltero/a, which can use either depending on context.

Model paragraph: En el futuro, me gustaría casarme y tener dos hijos. Mi boda ideal sería en la playa con toda mi familia. (In the future, I would like to get married and have two children. My ideal wedding would be on the beach with all my family.)
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for relationships and marriage
Master the conditional tense: infinitive + -ía endings
Memorise me gustaría + infinitive for 'I would like to'
Combine future time expressions with the near future and conditional

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — conditional tense and future plans are tested every year

steps.label: Step 2

steps.label: Step 2

bronze.question: Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning

gaps.correct_explain: gustaría is the conditional form of gustar. Me gustaría = I would like.

wrong.gusta: gusta is present tense (I like). You need the conditional → gustaría (I would like).
wrong.gustaba: gustaba is the imperfect (I used to like). The future context needs the conditional → gustaría.

gaps.correct_explain: tener is the infinitive. After me gustaría, always use the infinitive form.

wrong.tengo: tengo is the conjugated form (I have). After me gustaría, you need the infinitive → tener.
wrong.tendría: tendría is the conditional (I would have). After me gustaría, use the infinitive → tener.

gaps.correct_explain: casó is the él/ella preterite of casarse. Se casó = she got married.

wrong.casa: casa is present tense. El año pasado (last year) requires the preterite → se casó.
wrong.casará: casará is future tense. El año pasado is past → se casó.

gaps.correct_explain: casada agrees with hermana (feminine). Estar casada = to be married.

wrong.casarse: casarse is the infinitive. After estar, use the adjective → casada.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
silver.english: If I had the opportunity, I would live in Spain with my family.

gaps.rule: Imperfect subjunctive of tener after si
gaps.correct_explain: tuviera is the imperfect subjunctive of tener, used after si for hypothetical conditions.

wrong.tengo: tengo is present tense. After si for hypothetical situations, use the imperfect subjunctive → tuviera.
wrong.tendría: tendría is the conditional. After si, use the subjunctive → tuviera. The conditional goes in the other clause.

gaps.correct_explain: viviría is the conditional of vivir. In a si clause: si + subjunctive, conditional.

wrong.vivo: vivo is present tense. The hypothetical si clause requires the conditional → viviría.
wrong.viví: viví is preterite (I lived). A hypothetical situation needs the conditional → viviría.

gold.source_text: I think marriage is important because it shows commitment. However, I understand that nowadays many couples prefer not to get married. If I had the opportunity, I would live in Spain.
model_answers: Creo que el matrimonio es importante porque demuestra compromiso. Sin embargo, entiendo que hoy en día muchas parejas prefieren no casarse. Si tuviera la oportunidad, viviría en España.

gold.english: If I had the opportunity, I would get married on a beach.

distractor_labels.el: wrong gender — playa is feminine, so una not el
distractor_labels.caso: wrong form — caso is present tense, not conditional. You need casaría (I would get married)
distractor_labels.tengo: wrong tense — tengo is present. After si for hypothetical conditions, use tuviera (imperfect subjunctive)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are in a café in Spain with your exchange partner. They ask you about your future plans for relationships and family life. Answer in Spanish.

bullets.prompt: Say whether you want to get married and why.
bullets.model_answer: Me gustaría casarme algún día porque creo que el matrimonio es importante.
bullets.note: me gustaría + infinitive + opinion with porque

bullets.model_answer: Mi boda ideal sería en la playa con toda mi familia y mis amigos.

bullets.prompt: Ask your exchange partner what they think about marriage.
bullets.note: ¿Qué piensas sobre...? — question with inverted ¿ at start

bullets.prompt: Say what you would do if you had the opportunity.
bullets.model_answer: Si tuviera la oportunidad, viviría en España porque me encanta la cultura española.
bullets.note: si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional — Higher-level structure

gold.correct_text: Si tuviera la oportunidad, me casaría en una playa bonita con toda mi familia. Creo que el amor es lo más importante.
gold.translation: If I had the opportunity, I would get married on a beautiful beach with all my family. I think love is the most important thing.
